name: Syndromic Hair Shaft Abnormality
aliases: Hair Shaft Disorder with Systemic Features

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Syndromic Hair Shaft Abnormality Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Presence of characteristic hair shaft abnormalities confirmed by microscopic examination
Presence of at least one systemic feature such as dermatological, neurological, or immunological abnormalities
Identification of pathogenic variant in a gene known to cause syndromic hair shaft abnormalities
Exclusion of isolated hair shaft abnormalities without systemic involvement

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic hair shaft abnormalities plus at least one systemic feature
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation supports diagnosis but is not mandatory; diagnosis relies on clinical and microscopic findings.

pathognomonic.notes: Microscopic hair shaft defect characterized by nodes and fractures
Twisting of hair shafts leading to fragile hair

common.notes: Reduced hair density or sparse hair
Abnormalities in skin, nails, or teeth
Due to associated immunodeficiency in some syndromes
Mild to moderate cognitive impairment or motor delay

occasional.notes: Increased skin sensitivity to ultraviolet light
Hearing impairment due to inner ear involvement
Defective enamel formation leading to fragile teeth

rare.notes: Rare cardiac muscle involvement in some syndromes
Rare autoimmune involvement of thyroid gland

laboratory: Microscopic hair shaft analysis showing structural abnormalities (e.g., trichorrhexis nodosa, pili torti)
Immunological workup revealing immunodeficiency in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI may show nonspecific white matter changes in neurological involvement
Echocardiography for cardiomyopathy assessment if cardiac symptoms present
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as KRT81, KRT83, KRT86, or other hair shaft-related genes
Mutations in genes associated with syndromic ectodermal dysplasias
other: Clinical examination revealing ectodermal dysplasia features
Audiological testing for sensorineural hearing loss

distinguishingFeatures: Beaded hair shaft appearance without systemic involvement
Triangular hair shaft cross-section with no systemic abnormalities
Hair is unruly but no associated ectodermal defects

redFlags: Rapid progression of hair fragility with systemic symptoms
references: Orphanet: Syndromic Hair Shaft Abnormality - ORPHA:79367
Traupe H, et al. Hair shaft disorders: clinical and genetic aspects. J Am Acad Dermatol. 2017.
Patel A, et al. Syndromic hair shaft abnormalities: diagnosis and management. Clin Dermatol. 2022.
